event: # fmo-events.tsv -- what the SERVER does with a script's server call (0x0159).
# A lobby script calls syscall 0xE220 {event, params[16]}; the client sends the
# record as 0x0159 and the script's 0xE222 reads the 16 params back out of the
# record AFTER our reply -- so SE's server answered by pushing the processed
# record in 0x015A (+0xAD8 = 0) and then acking. The rule for each event lived
# on SE's server and is not in the client; this file is where it lives now.
# Columns (tab-separated):
#   event   the u32 at record+0x000 (decimal or 0x..)
#   p1      the first param the row matches, or * for any
#   answer  pN=<expr>[;pN=<expr>]   rewrite param N in the answered record;
#           <expr> = int | pM | flag[pM] | flag[<idx>]  (the pilot's flag byte)
#   set     FMO_STATUS_FLAGS grammar on the pilot's flags: 128=99 (byte), 173
#           (bit); pM is allowed as an index, so p1=99 = "set the byte the
#           script named to 99"
#   note    free text, logged when the row fires
# A row that changes nothing for a pilot is a plain ack. Rows starting with #
# are comments. There are NO active rows shipped: every candidate below is
# INFERRED from the captures + the missions table and enabling one is a live
# test whose bar is the script's next branch, not the log line.
# The helper library (D87/D63/D65 0x740..) classifies the events by whether the script
# READS the answer (fmoscriptdis, 2026-09-11):
#   NOTIFY (one arg, answer never read): 200, 201, 204, 205, 208 -- server-side effects
# So a `set` row fits a NOTIFY event and an `answer` row fits a QUERY event.
# What the captures say (logs/captures/fmo-0159-*.bin, 2026-09-05..09-11):
#   101  []               at lobby entry (srv_101 in every script's helper
#                         library, AI/F00/D87.DAT 0x740): the script tests the
#                         answered p1 != 0 and only then runs a second call.
#   104  [130]            Kwangsu Son: 130 = own_byte of "Enemy Unit
#                         Annihilation" (fmo-missions.tsv). srv_104(p) RETURNS
#                         the answered p1 to its caller. Candidate: the server

#   205  [34, 104, 130]   the senior sergeant (tag_senior / registration)
#   102  [0, row, col, a, b]  a sector (row*1000+col tile) -- the war map
